did: Home now counts every request it makes to the outside. Every HTTP client in file_host and its crates is built by one constructor, crates/outbound, for a closed list of callers, and each request is recorded once by caller, host and outcome, with its wait and its bytes; clippy and a test refuse a client built any other way. A new OUTBOUND dashboard draws it, with every container's network beside it from cadvisor. On the way, home's cadvisor turned out to name no container at all, so WHO DUNNIT's container panels summed every cgroup into one false bar: cadvisor now reads dockerd's own containerd, and an unnamed cgroup is left out instead of summed. Two alerts the owner asked for: a host that stops answering one of home's workers, and ESPN refusing the game feed for half an hour. It merged as server#1070; the ledger's home-outbound family and the calls landed in some-ui#3398.

calls.title: One constructor for every outbound HTTP client, in a new small crate (C890)
options: one constructor in a new small crate, crates/outbound, wrapping reqwest with a closed Caller enum
reqwest-middleware's ClientWithMiddleware with a metrics middleware, Caller carried as an extension
keep each client where it is and add a counter at each of the eight sites
calls.why: The issue asks for one constructor 'in an existing crate if one fits' but no existing crate owns HTTP: some-metrics' README rules measurement out, and the kits are per-service adapters. reqwest-middleware is the outsourced answer C787 prefers, and the cost against it (its error type rippling through every caller) is a judgement on the size of the ripple, not a rule. Every HTTP client in file_host and its crates is built by one constructor, outbound::client(Caller), in a new small crate, crates/outbound.
calls.undo: Point the kits' ReqwestTransport back at reqwest::Client, restore the per-site builders and delete crates/outbound; or swap the wrapper for reqwest-middleware behind the same Caller enum.

calls.title: The host label is a fixed name per caller, never read from a URL (C891)
options: a closed Host enum fixed per caller by Caller::host
the request URL's host mapped into a closed set at send time, other for the rest
calls.why: The issue says host is fixed per caller, but Notice reaches two Google hosts and Nudge reaches whichever push service each browser uses, so one fixed name per caller merges hosts that a URL-derived label would split. The host label is a closed Host enum, fixed per caller by Caller::host, never read from a URL: espn, github_raw (call_weeks and cards_essays together), mailbox_worker, googleapis (FCM's oauth2 and fcm hosts as one), web_push (every browser's push service as one, since the endpoint is per browser), loopback.
calls.undo: Split a caller into two cases (Notice into token and send) if one host needs telling apart.

calls.title: Measuring an outbound request ends at the answer's headers (C892)
options: measure to the answer's headers and count declared Content-Length, saying so where the numbers are read
return a counting wrapper around reqwest::Response so body failures and bytes actually read are recorded
fold game_feed_fetches_total into the generic series
calls.why: Nothing said where a request ends. The wrapper is more exact, but it changes the Response type every caller reads its body from (the game feed's capped chunk reads, the kits' bytes and text) for a difference only a body that stalls after its headers shows; and the issue leaves the game feed's own series to keep or fold. Measuring ends at the answer's headers: outcome (ok, refused_4xx, refused_5xx, timeout, no_answer) and duration are taken when send returns, and bytes received are the declared Content-Length, read or not.
calls.undo: Return a counting wrapper around reqwest::Response from Request::send and record on drop.

calls.title: A clippy ban plus a test refuse any other way to build a client (C893)
options: clippy disallowed-methods on the reqwest constructors and ClientBuilder::build, plus a test refusing the reqwest::Client type outside the crate
calls.why: The issue offers either clippy or a grep test. Clippy cannot name a trait method, so Client::default() passes it (verified); a grep alone misses a builder never named by type. Neither closes an alias like use reqwest as r. The check is two-part.
calls.undo: Drop the test if clippy gains trait-method paths.

calls.title: cadvisor pointed at dockerd's own containerd; unnamed cgroups left out of the panels (C894)
options: leave unnamed cgroups out with name!="" and point cadvisor at dockerd's containerd with --containerd
label unnamed series by their cgroup id instead
leave the panels and wait for a cadvisor release
calls.why: The dashboards assumed cadvisor's name label is always there, and home's cadvisor gave none. The fix touches WHO DUNNIT's panels and home's monitoring config, which the task named only through the OUTBOUND container row; and the suggested --containerd-namespace=moby turned out, in cadvisor's source, to be read by the containerd factory, not the Docker one. Home's cadvisor names no container (the owner's check on 2026-11-21: only cgroup ids), so every name=~"$container" matcher also requires name!="".
calls.undo: Drop the name!="" matchers once cadvisor names containers again; they are harmless left in.

left: No OUTBOUND clip: this session could not write to paulgsc/testing, so the dashboard's stills are still owed (some-ui#3405).
The cadvisor fix is not yet seen on home: after the next deploy, cadvisor's log should say Registering Docker factory and OUTBOUND's CONTAINERS NAMED stat should stop reading gray (some-ui#3404).
Bytes received are declared lengths, and measuring ends at the answer's headers: a body that stalls after them counts as its status. Said in the crate doc, the dashboard and the README.
The mailbox bell is a WebSocket, not HTTP, so it is not on the outbound series; its bytes are in the container row.
